What is the difference between an Online+ degree and a regular online degree?

Online+ degrees include enhanced support such as proactive advising, structured course sequencing, and student engagement, while traditional online programs are more self-directed. Additionally, Online+ degrees have the added benefit of offering a free, fast-track application process, 8-week terms, and microcredential options.

Can you tell me more about your online programs?

TTU Online offers a wide range of undergraduate and graduate degrees designed for flexibility, accessibility, and career alignment, delivered in accelerated 8-week formats. We have programs in the social sciences, pre-health, business, leadership, communication, etc.

If I was in a two year college and was not able to finish due to some unforseen circumstances, would online+ be something that I can do to get my degree?

Yes, the Texas Tech Online+ program offers flexible options for non-traditional students who may have been unable to finish their degree due to unforeseen circumstances. If you have prior college credits, we have a team of Online Degree Pathway Specialists who can review their credits and provide a sample degree plan for their desired online major.

Online Bachelor of Applied Arts & Sciences in Applied Leadership

A flexible, career-focused degree designed for working adults, military personnel and transfer students looking to complete their education and advance their careers.

The online Bachelor of Applied Arts & Sciences (BAAS) in Applied Leadership from Texas Tech University offers a pathway for students with prior college credits or an Associate of Applied Science (AAS) degree to advance their careers through a flexible and interdisciplinary curriculum.

This program is ideal for nontraditional learners, including working professionals and military personnel, seeking a degree that aligns with their busy lives and career aspirations. With competitive tuition rates, opportunities to earn credit for work and life experience, and specialized concentrations, the BAAS degree prepares you for roles in human resources, project management, business administration and beyond.

Online Bachelor of Applied Arts & Sciences in Human Sciences

Transform your career and make a lasting impact in healthcare, family services and wellness with Texas Tech University’s Bachelor of Applied Arts & Sciences in Human Sciences—available fully online or in a hybrid format on campus in Lubbock. Designed for working adults, this flexible degree helps you fast-track your education and leverage real-world experience for career advancement.

The Bachelor of Applied Arts & Sciences (BAAS) in Human Sciences is an interdisciplinary degree designed to help you build on your professional experience, integrate your vocational skills with academic knowledge, and accelerate your career. Offered fully online or in a hybrid format on campus in Lubbock, this degree provides flexibility to complete coursework while managing family and work commitments. With a focus on multiple fields within the College of Health & Human Sciences, you can tailor your education to your career goals by choosing from three areas of concentration, including Addictive Disorders and Nutritional Sciences—allowing you to design a path that aligns with your passions and aspirations. The career-oriented curriculum prepares you for a variety of roles in health care administration, human resources, nonprofit leadership, and more, making it ideal for those looking to apply their work experience in meaningful ways. With the ability to transfer up to 60 hours from your Associate of Applied Science (AAS) degree, you can complete your bachelor’s in as little as two years and advance quickly in your career.

Designed for working professionals and nontraditional students, this flexible program offers hands-on learning, expert faculty, and opportunities to earn credit for prior work-life experience. Whether you’re advancing in your current role or pursuing new career opportunities, TTU’s Online BBA prepares you to lead, innovate, and thrive. What is a time ticket?

This is a specific date and time window that is assigned to you that will allow you to register for classes. You can find your Time Ticket by following the steps below:

Step 1: Login to Raiderlink (opens in new tab)

Will tuition change?

Tuition remains charged on a per-credit basis (unless otherwise specified by the program). The cost per credit is not changed simply because of the 8-week structure.

Overall program cost remains comparable to the traditional format.

How do I enroll in a payment plan?

How to Enroll into a Payment Plan (opens in new tab):

Step 1: Login to Raiderlink (opens in new tab)

Step 2: Select the MyTech tab from the left-hand side menu and then select Student Business Services

Step 3: Under Student Business Services select eBill

Step 4: Select Payment Plans

Step 5: Select Enroll Now

Step 6: Select the appropriate term from the Select a term drop-down and click Select

Available payment plans and a summary overview will be displayed. You may select "Details" for a full description of the payment plan.

Step 1: Click Select for the desired payment plan

The payment plan installments will be displayed with dates and amounts.

Step 1: Make selection for automatic payments & then click Continue

Step 2: Select a payment method from the drop-down menu

Step 3: Select Continue, The Payment Plan Agreement will be displayed. Review the terms and conditions. Select the I agree to the payment plan agreement button and then select Continue

Step 4: Confirm your payment selection, transaction details, and payment details

Step 5: Enter your personal information and bank information, then select Continue

Step 6: If the payment is successful, you will receive confirmation of payment and a receipt.

Step 7: If a payment confirmation page and receipt was not received, please navigate to the Payment Plan tab to verify if enrollment was successful or contact Student Business Services.

Tuition Estimator:

To calculate an estimate on your tuition and fees for the term, please utilize Tuition Estimator (opens in new tab). Cost for housing, food, books, and other personal expenses are not included.

How much does the 10-K program cost? Are there additional fees?

The total cost is $10,000.00 or less for qualified students. There is a $2,000.00 conversion fee for the 21 hours earned through microcredentials and prior learning experience credits. Students are then billed per credit hour at Texas Tech for remaining course work.

You can get started in the first four micro-credential courses for free and pay later when you convert them to credit.  Also, all eligible prior-learning credits will convert to credit for no cost.

Your advisor will connect you with a financial aid advisor to discuss all financing options.

How much do the degrees cost?

Costs vary by program, but Online+ is designed to be competitive and transparent. https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/affordable/.

Can Financial Aid cover the $2,000.00 fee?

The $2,000.00 fee is an out of pocket expense.

Doctor of Philosophy in Technical Communication and Rhetoric

The PhD in Technical Communication & Rhetoric (TCR) is designed for students with an interest in rhetoric, writing, technical communication, and composition. The aim of this doctoral program is to engage the students in acquiring broad knowledge of the history, theory, research, genres, and practice of technical communication and rhetoric; specialized knowledge of some aspect of communication or rhetoric; and ability to conduct independent research.

The program emphasizes five broad areas in its scholarship, coursework, and initiatives:

Step 1: Rhetoric, Composition, and Technology

Step 2: Technical Communication

Step 3: Rhetorics of Science and Healthcare

Step 4: Technology, Culture, and Rhetoric

Step 5: Visual Rhetoric, New Media, and User-Centered Design

If I need to withdraw from a course that is not required, will that count towards my withdraw amounts that I am allowed, even if it was told that I needed it and then later told that it is not required?

You should always check in with your Online Student Advocate regarding any course withdrawals to understand the implications fully. Additionally, it's essential to review the Academic and Financial Calendars to determine any consequences of withdrawing. If you feel that you were recommended a course that you did not need, please let your Online Student Advocate know immediately so they can explore options to support you.

When it comes to withdrawals, they can count towards limits set by your institution, so discussing this specific situation with your Online Student Advocate will provide clarity on how it affects your allowed withdraw amounts.

Remember, before making any decisions, consider discussing the financial consequences of withdrawing with your financial aid advisor.

**Tuition Costs at Texas Tech University Online**

- **Per-Credit Basis**: Tuition is charged on a per-credit basis, and the cost per credit does not change due to the program's structure. The overall program cost remains comparable to the traditional format.

- **10-K Program**: The total cost is $10,000 or less for qualified students. There is a $2,000 conversion fee for the 21 hours earned through microcredentials and prior learning experience credits. Students are billed per credit hour for the remaining coursework.

- **Program-Specific Costs**: Costs vary by program, but Online+ is designed to be competitive and transparent. More information on specific program costs can be found at [TTU Online Affordable](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/affordable/).

- **Tuition Estimator**: To calculate an estimate of your tuition and fees for the term, you can use the Tuition Estimator available on the TTU website.

For further details or specific inquiries, you can contact TTU Online at 1-844-691-0494 or email online@ttu.edu.
